messages:
incident-bot: Paging raj_oncall (on-call) for SEV: elevated 5xx in northshore region — >10% error rate on gateway tier, automated throttle triggered. Escalation policy: page on-call and #incidents.
raj_oncall: I'm awake, looking. joining bridge in 2. :wave:
maria_g: seeing a sudden spike in 502/504 from northshore-gateway-01..04, started ~08:22 UTC. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ingress/northshore?from=now-30m
tony_r: logs show a lot of "connection reset by peer" and "upstream: timed out" from proxy -> egress-nat. sample:
```
[08:23:11] proxy northshore-gw-02 ERROR upstream request failed: read tcp 10.0.3.5:443: read: connection reset by peer
[08:23:12] gateway northshore-gw-03 WARN upstream timeout after 10s
```
jess_ops: can someone check NAT connection pool utilization? pinging infra.
infra-bot: NAT pool northshore-1: connections=1240/1200 (exhausted), retries=324, last_scale_event=+3h
raj_oncall: ok NAT connect exhaustion looks plausible. rolling oncall runbook step 1: route traffic away from northshore pool to fallback region and scale nat if possible. leo_prod please coordinate with traffic team for policy steer.
leo_prod: already flagged to traffic routing. initiating cross-region steer to westshore (soft steer) — 10% increments. url: https://routing.console/redwood/steer/alpha
sam_support: Customer impact: 4 customers reporting latency/502s on their dashboards (support ticket IDs: #4320, #4321, #4323). Notifying top 10 customers with affected region note.
maria_g: starting quick probe to verify KV cache vs nat issue. `curl` to edge -> internal service shows 200 for cached keys, but 502 for new connections. suggests upstream connectivity problem.
raj_oncall: runbook says fallback: enable backup gateway pool (northshore-backup) and expand connection timeout. Doing that now: 
```
# enable backup pool
curl -XPOST -sS https://api.internal.redwood/infra/pools/northshore/backup/enable -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
infra-bot: northshore-backup pool enabled, healthchecks passing (3/3), routing weight applied: backup=20%
tony_r: also temporarily lowering gateway circuit-breaker threshold to reduce retries -> reduce fanout. patch:
```
circuit_breaker.max_concurrent_requests = 100
circuit_breaker.max_retries = 1
```
jess_ops: NAT team reports a misconfigured health check on natgw autoscale that caused slow scale-up. they pushed a hotfix to scale policy (min-conns -> 2x) and triggered immediate scale.
infra-bot: NAT pool northshore-1 scaled to 3 nodes (from 1). connection capacity now 3600.
maria_g: error-rate graph dropping after steer to westshore and backup pool activation. current northshore 5xx = 6% (was 18%). customer-reported 502s decreased.
raj_oncall: good. keep steer in place until NAT pool stabilizes for 20 minutes. I'll update pagerduty and start incident timeline.
sam_support: posting interim customer comms: "We're actively mitigating elevated 5xx errors in Northshore. Traffic is being temporarily routed to a nearby region while we restore capacity. We'll update in 30 minutes." :phone:
leo_prod: can we enable degraded-mode caching as a knee-jerk to reduce new upstream connections? set ttl for certain endpoints to 60s.
maria_g: enabling prefix KV caching on high-traffic routes. patch applied.
```
# example cache config
routes:/api/v1/generate/cache_ttl=60
```
tony_r: post-fix logs show decreased upstream timeouts and fewer resets. rolling out wider routing revert in 5m increments.
raj_oncall: re-evaluating impact: current metrics -> request latency stable, 5xx trending to normal. still monitoring for any residues (rate-limited customers at edge still seeing 502).
jess_ops: recommend post-incident action items: 1) tighten NAT autoscale test coverage, 2) add synthetic probes for conn exhaustion, 3) add per-pool connection metrics to dashboard.
sam_support: created support playbook entry and updated customers. ticket #4320/#4321 assigned to sam_support for postmortem comms.
leo_prod: I'll coordinate follow-up with traffic and infra to remove the temporary steer after verifying capacity. ETA 40m.
raj_oncall: handing off to day-shift SRE (maria_g) at 09:15 UTC for monitoring and follow-through. I'll draft incident summary and runbook deviations.
maria_g: ack taking 1st-line for next 60m. will capture all logs and start timeline.
raj_oncall: incident status -> mitigated (partial) at 08:59 UTC, still monitoring. next update in 30m or on any regression. :lock:
infra-bot: auto-note: incident ticket INC-2026-193 created, severity: high, assigned: infra-team, timeline link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-193
jess_ops: thanks all — great coordination. please file RCA notes and add playbook PRs.
sam_support: will send customer follow-up summary after RCA.
raj_oncall: closing page. follow-ups: RCA, test coverage, synthetic probes, failure-injection test to simulate NAT conn exhaustion. tagging for postmortem: @leo_prod @jess_ops @tony_r @maria_g @infra-team
maria_g: noting runbook deviation: used backup pool instead of full region evac. will include justification in RCA."
